method: static only, zero network: E392's population, resolver and statuses are imported and its scan is called with one function swapped -- a face above MAX_FACE_BYTES is read in 8 MB chunks and asked, byte-wise, whether it stores the key. Nothing about the resolver is re-implemented; the published face is read from disk to state the baseline the delta is measured against.
refusals: a raw hit claims presence, never structure: it is published under its own marker
the byte matcher cannot see through escapes, so a key name inside a string value is not a hit -- the same asymmetry E392's parsed test has in the other direction
the uncapped run is re-derived from today's tree, so its name-matched total differs from the published one by tree drift; that drift is published, not subtracted
faces that do not parse stay refused -- the cap is the only refusal removed here
the study does not scan itself, its face, its mirror or its smoke leg

summary.site_corpus: e391.py_corpus (the same walk that produced the key population)

verify_covers: both shares re-divide from the per-key rows and the name-matched total
the cap arithmetic closes: stores_with_cap + hidden_storing == stores_without_cap
every example row names a key that has a per-key row and a face the scan opened
the verdict re-derives from the published cap numbers
verify_does_not_cover: the corpus walk and the byte scan themselves
whether a raw presence claim holds at the depth the site indexes
